problem: Learning-based ImageNav needs millions of simulator trials and generalizes poorly, while exploration-based methods (frontier, stubborn, semantic-map methods like MOPA/GaussNav) lack learning from past observations and become inefficient in complex environments.
motivation: ImageNav matters for search and rescue and home robots, where the target may be out of sight or behind obstacles. The paper argues that a photorealistic scene prior that can render future views, combined with Bayesian belief updates, can give efficient exploration and navigation without training data or experience.
key_idea: Formulate ImageNav as an optimal control problem solved by Monte Carlo MPC, using 3D Gaussian Splatting to render predicted future observations and a Bayesian search-theory update of the target-location belief driven by image similarity.
insight: Rendering candidate future views from 3DGS lets the planner score rollouts by expected image similarity and exploration cost, replacing learned policies. The ablation (Fig. 4, hard scenes) shows both parts are needed: without Bayesian updating, the MC-MPC does not converge to a location; with Bayesian updating only, it converges to a wrong location; the full method reaches the lowest NE in the fewest steps.
method: Problem formulation: ImageNav as a discrete HJB optimal control cost: terminal image dissimilarity plus a sum of one-step exploration costs, cost = movement cost / (belief mass × prior success rate) from optimal search theory.

Process-aware Bayesian update: the search area is divided into M cells; after each observation without a match, the cell probability mass is updated by p_i(1-q_i)/(1-p_i q_i) and the other cells are renormalized. q_i is set to 1 minus the VLAD (AnyLoc-VLAD-DINO) descriptor distance between the observation and the goal image.

3DGS view prediction: a 3DGS map (splatfacto, built from 534 posed images) renders the predicted image at any pose. A blimp motion model (4-DoF, one active control at a time) rolls out N trajectories of horizon K.
Rollout scoring: weight w = exp(-J), where J is the terminal image dissimilarity plus the exploration cost along the rollout.

Monte Carlo MPC: sequential importance resampling of the control distribution, approximating a KL-minimizing optimal distribution (MPPI/CEM-like), with added noise to avoid degeneracy. Only the first control of the best sequence is applied, then the loop repeats with new observations.

setting.backbone: AnyLoc-VLAD-DINO descriptors (frozen) for image similarity + 3DGS (splatfacto) scene map; no learned policy
setting.training_data: none (no policy training); 3DGS fit per scene from 534 posed RGB images (1920x1440), which also form the VPR database
setting.action_space: continuous 4-DoF body-frame velocities (vx, vy, vz, yaw rate), one nonzero at a time; discrete steps
setting.simulator: custom 3DGS-rendered map (real indoor 10x10x2 m test field), no standard simulator
setting.privileged: pre-built 3DGS map of the test scene with metric poses (OptiTrack-captured) and known motion model; OptiTrack pose tracking in real-world runs

numbers.eval_set_note: 50 trials from a fixed initial pose per difficulty level, run in 3DGS map
numbers.extra: custom indoor scene; success = entering Last-Mile stage within 50 steps; NS is min number of steps

numbers.eval_set_note: 50 trials, three 1.5 m obstacles, long distance

numbers_note: Only a self-built blimp benchmark (three difficulty levels in one indoor room), not a standard ImageNav benchmark. The ablation appears only as a figure. Real-world results are qualitative.
results: On the custom blimp benchmark, BEINGS gets 100/100/78% SR on Easy/Medium/Hard, with SPC 0.98/0.73/0.53. The strongest baseline on easy/medium is the VPR database + frontier (100% SR, but SPC 0.87/0.56, NS 5/37). On Hard, the frontier, stubborn and uniform baselines fail to finish within 50 steps, and the best directly-approach baseline (VPR database) reaches only 64% SR with SPC 0.00.
limitations: Requires a pre-built, metrically posed 3DGS map of the scene, so it is not truly unseen-environment navigation.
Evaluated only on a small self-built indoor blimp benchmark (50 trials per level) with no standard ImageNav benchmark comparison; the Hard SR is 78%.
Depends on known motion and measurement models and OptiTrack tracking; per-step compute is high (GPU rendering), and the authors say GPU acceleration and self-localization remain future work.
builds_on: Bayesian search/process-aware Bayesian update (Li et al. 2021)
